title: Weimar Germany 1918-29: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the people and rules of Germany's new republic after WWI.
meta_desc: GCSE History Weimar 1918-29 foundations — abdication, constitution, Versailles.

walkthroughs.body_html:
On 9 November 1918 Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated as Germany lost WWI.

The Social Democrat leader Friedrich Ebert took charge. Germany became a republic. Two days later, the war ended.

In August 1919 Germany got a new constitution.

All adults over 20 could vote. The Reichstag was elected by proportional representation. A President was elected separately — and held emergency power under Article 48.

The Treaty of Versailles in June 1919 forced Germany to accept war guilt.

It lost 13% of its land, all colonies, most of its army and owed huge reparations. Many Germans called it a 'Diktat' — a forced peace.

mcqs.q: What caused the German hyperinflation of 1923?
options: Reparations alone caused the hyperinflation.
The government printing money to pay striking workers during the French occupation of the Ruhr, on top of existing reparations and war debts.
The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.

mcqs.q: Why did the Treaty of Versailles cause resentment in Germany?
options: Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
It assigned sole war guilt to Germany (Article 231) and imposed harsh reparations, territorial losses and military restrictions.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
Because Germany lost more soldiers than any other country in the war.

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
